title: You don’t stay stuck by accident.
paragraphs: You don’t stay stuck by accident.
It happens quietly… slowly… almost respectfully.
You still show up. You still say the words. You still call yourself a Christian.
But something inside you hasn’t moved in a long time.
And if no one says it plainly, you could live your whole life thinking you’re growing—when you’ve actually been standing still.
There are patterns to spiritual stagnation. Not random failures—patterns. And once you see them, you can’t unsee them.
Some of these might feel uncomfortably familiar.
Not because this is attacking you.
Because it’s exposing what’s been hiding in you.
The first one is the Christian who listens… but never changes.
You hear sermons. You save posts. You nod at truth.
You even feel something when the Word hits.

James didn’t soften this when he wrote:
“Be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.” — James 1:22
You thought you were growing because you were consuming.
You knew what God said about that habit.
You knew what He was calling you to surrender.
But you delayed it. Just a little longer. Just one more time.
And that “little longer” became your lifestyle.
Then there’s the Christian who replaces relationship with routine.
You read Scripture—but it’s a checklist.
You attend church—but your heart isn’t there.

Jesus warned about this kind of closeness without intimacy:
“This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.” — Matthew 15:8
That’s not distance caused by ignorance.
You learned how to look alive spiritually…
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
God is not impressed by routines that replace Him.
Then there’s the Christian who protects their sin instead of killing it.
You’ve learned how to justify it.

Romans 6:12 says:
“Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, to make you obey its passions.”
And every time you chose it, something in you hardened just a little more.
Then there’s the Christian who waits… but never moves.
You say you’re waiting on God.
You already know what He said.

James 4:17 cuts through it:
“So whoever knows the right thing to do and fails to do it, for him it is sin.”
Then there’s the Christian who wants blessing… without surrender.
But you don’t want the death that comes before resurrection.

Jesus didn’t hide this:
“If anyone would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily and follow me.” — Luke 9:23
You wanted God to add to your life…
But not take anything from it.
And that’s why you feel stuck.
Because transformation only comes after surrender.
And then… there’s the most dangerous one.
The Christian who thinks they’re fine.

Revelation 3:16 says:
“Because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I will spit you out of my mouth.”
That’s written to people who think they’re okay.
You’re just not pursuing Him either.
And that middle ground is where spiritual life slowly dies.
Here’s the tension you’ve been avoiding.
A surrender that finally says, “No more pretending.”
Because the Gospel isn’t just that Jesus forgives sin.
It’s that He breaks its power.

Romans 5:8 says:
“God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”

And 2 Corinthians 5:17 declares:
“If anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away; behold, the new has come.”
That means stuck is not your identity.
But staying there… is a choice.
And right now, you feel it.
That sense that this wasn’t just words…
If you know which one you’ve been…
But if you’re ready, you can even write it here.
And if this hit you, don’t keep it to yourself. Someone in your life is trapped in the same silence. Share this with them. Let it interrupt them the way it just interrupted you.
Follow this journey if you’re tired of surface-level faith and want truth that actually transforms. Save this—because conviction fades when distraction returns.
And if you’re ready to go deeper—real growth, real correction, real discipleship—step into it here:
But freedom… will cost you everything.
